headline: No option wins outright: each step up in overall quality, from Brisk-S to Atlas-M to Atlas-L, costs more per point, and nothing declared says which price is worth paying.
lede: Atlas-L scores higher than Atlas-M on overall quality in every live task, at {cost.gap.atlas-l.atlas-m.multiple} its cost; Atlas-M holds the safety-type conduct checks that the cheaper models miss. A declared price per point, or a quality floor per task, would turn this into a decision.

caveats.material_if: Material to the pick whatever the figures say: no gate, floor or price per point was declared, so which option to run is the concierge owner's choice; the measured trade itself does not rest on it.

Only if pairing would reorder the options: every gap here is read unpaired, which is wider than a paired reading where models share cases. Pairing would likely narrow the price bands rather than reverse a step, but it could settle whether Open-70B joins the cheap end of the frontier.
Only if a re-run on fresh cases pulled Atlas-L's lead over Atlas-M down far enough to move the price band of that step; the lead is clear of zero in each live task.

Only if the unnamed judge of the conduct checks is more lenient on the Atlas models than on Brisk-S or Open-70B; our lean toward Atlas-M rests on those checks, while overall quality comes from a calibrated judge.

decision.text: Brisk-S is the cheapest at {cost_per_1k.brisk-s} per 1,000 conversations; Atlas-M costs {cost.gap.atlas-m.brisk-s.multiple} as much and scores higher on overall quality; Atlas-L costs {cost.gap.atlas-l.atlas-m.multiple} as much as Atlas-M and scores higher again. Open-70B is off the frontier on point estimates only: its gain over Brisk-S ({price.brisk-s.open-70b.overall.gain_interval_unpaired} points) is not told apart from zero.

Brisk-S is the pick while a point of overall quality is worth less than {price.brisk-s.atlas-m.overall.per_point_low_unpaired} to {price.brisk-s.atlas-m.overall.per_point_high_unpaired} per 1,000 conversations; Atlas-M above that band and below {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.per_point_low_unpaired} to {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.per_point_high_unpaired}; Atlas-L above it. Inside the first band Open-70B is also a contender, and inside either band this run does not settle the pick. The bands treat cost as exact.

Our lean, not a recommendation: Atlas-M, for a point priced between the bands. It is not told apart from Atlas-L on any conduct check, while Brisk-S and Open-70B fall behind it on confirming account changes, unsupported claims, resolving issues and declining to speculate.

Cost carries no interval, no count of trials that reported it, and no named provider, so the cost order holds for this run's unknown routing. The conduct checks come from a judge the campaign does not name. Speculation bait carries no traffic: its rates are a test of behaviour under bait, not what live traffic meets.

The concierge owner declares a price per point of overall quality, or a floor on it in every task, saying whether speculation bait counts; either picks one option from the figures already measured, unless the price lands inside a band.

claims.text: A point of overall quality costs more on the step from Atlas-M to Atlas-L than on the step from Brisk-S to Atlas-M, and the price bands of the two steps do not overlap while cost is read as exact.

evidence.caption: Price per point per 1,000 conversations along the frontier, banded by the quality gain's unpaired interval only. Pooled overall quality reads {pooled.overall.brisk-s.mean} for Brisk-S, {pooled.overall.open-70b.mean} for Open-70B, {pooled.overall.atlas-m.mean} for Atlas-M and {pooled.overall.atlas-l.mean} for Atlas-L, so the steps gain {price.brisk-s.atlas-m.overall.gain} ({price.brisk-s.atlas-m.overall.gain_interval_unpaired}) and {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.gain} ({price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.gain_interval_unpaired}) points for {price.brisk-s.atlas-m.overall.cost_gap|abs} and {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.cost_gap|abs} more. Cost carries no interval and is priced under this run's unnamed provider routing: the bands would meet only if the Atlas-M to Atlas-L cost gap shrank, or the Brisk-S to Atlas-M gap grew, until {price.brisk-s.atlas-m.overall.per_point_high_unpaired} and {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.per_point_low_unpaired} touched.

claims.text: Atlas-L scores higher than Atlas-M on overall quality in every live task, by most in troubleshooting ({compare.atlas-l.atlas-m.overall.task.trouble.difference|abs} points); on speculation bait, which carries no traffic, the two are not told apart.

evidence.caption: Atlas-L less Atlas-M on overall quality, one row per task with unpaired intervals and no pooled row; pooled over the live tasks the gap is {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.gain} ({price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.gain_interval_unpaired}).

claims.text: Atlas-M is not told apart from Atlas-L on any conduct check; the cheaper models fall behind it on the safety-type checks, with Open-70B confirming before account changes {compare.atlas-m.open-70b.confirms.task.trouble.difference|abs} points less often, but not on every check.

evidence.caption: The checks where both cheaper models fall behind Atlas-M, each in the task that tests it, with intervals; speculation bait carries no traffic share.

The other checks: Open-70B is not told apart from Atlas-M on staying in character ({compare.open-70b.atlas-m.character.task.persona.interval}), clear steps or escalating; Brisk-S on clear steps ({compare.brisk-s.atlas-m.steps.task.trouble.interval}) or citing the source, where its gap's interval ends at zero.

claims.text: Atlas-L is also the slowest in every task: on research-needed questions its p95 latency is {task.research.atlas-l.latency_s.p95}, against {task.research.atlas-m.latency_s.p95} for Atlas-M.

evidence.caption: Latency from median to p95, by task; no latency budget was declared.

explore.control: Price of one point of overall quality, per 1,000 conversations
explore.binds: Which frontier option is the best buy
explore.outcome: On point estimates: Brisk-S below {price.brisk-s.atlas-m.overall.per_point_low_unpaired} to {price.brisk-s.atlas-m.overall.per_point_high_unpaired}; Atlas-M from there to {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.per_point_low_unpaired} to {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.per_point_high_unpaired}; Atlas-L above. Within the first band Open-70B could be the buy: a point bought from it on to Atlas-M costs {price.open-70b.atlas-m.overall.per_point_low_unpaired} to {price.open-70b.atlas-m.overall.per_point_high_unpaired}.

method.text: {scoreboard.atlas-m.cases} cases per model across the tasks listed in the appendix; repeats are not stated. No model lost or failed a trial.

An ordinal score from a judge calibrated on {judged.overall.calibration_ratings} human ratings, agreeing {judged.overall.agreement}. Each model's overall figure is pooled over the {pooled.overall.atlas-l.slices|words} live tasks, weighted by traffic share; speculation bait carries {task.specul.share} of traffic and is left out of it.

Pass or fail checks, each read in the one task that tests it; the campaign does not say who judged them or how they were calibrated. Confirming account changes, resolving issues, unsupported claims and declining to speculate are called the safety-type checks here.

At the {compare.atlas-l.atlas-m.overall.task.trouble.level} level, uncorrected. With no control, every gap between two models combines each model's own interval as if they ran different cases, which reads wider than a paired interval.
Cost per 1,000 conversations as measured, read as exact; no provider is named for any model, no count of trials reporting a cost is stated, and no monthly volume is declared.

The cost gap between two neighbouring frontier options over their gain in pooled overall quality; its band comes from the gain's unpaired interval alone. Open-70B is left off the frontier on point estimates and named as a contender where its interval allows.
Median and p95 per task; no latency budget was declared.
No control, gate, floor, margin or price per point; {n_candidates|words} models compared as equals.
